user_input: Compare AA24-109A and AA25-071A: which actors are reported using Rclone, and how do their advisory software-to-technique mappings compare? Cite both reports and keep each mapping within its source context.
response:
BianLian group actors use Rclone to exfiltrate data. [E6, E9]
LockBit affiliates use Rclone to exfiltrate data. [E12]
BianLian group uses File Transfer Protocol (FTP) and Rclone to exfiltrate data. [E9]
LockBit affiliates use MEGA for data exfiltration. [E12]
BianLian group uses Exfiltration to Cloud Storage (T1567.002). [E9]
LockBit affiliates use Transfer Data to Cloud Account (T1537). [E12]
BianLian group uses Rclone, a tool used to sync files to cloud storage. [E9]
LockBit affiliates use Rclone, an open-source command line cloud storage manager or FreeFileSync to exfiltrate. [E12]

reference: AA24-109A reports Akira threat actors using Rclone, with advisory mappings T1048; AA25-071A reports Medusa actors using Rclone, with advisory mappings T1567.002. These mappings describe the cited reports and do not establish that every use of the software has these behaviors. The Akira report cites T1048 (Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol); the Medusa report cites T1567.002 (Exfiltration to Cloud Storage). These are distinct source-reported mappings for the same software.
